newsitem.title: ITALY: UNITA says ready for Angola peace summit in Italy.
newsitem.headline: UNITA says ready for Angola peace summit in Italy.

text.p: The leader of Angola's opposition movement UNITA, Jonas Savimbi, is ready to hold talks in Italy with President Jose Eduardo dos Santos to try to end fighting in northeastern Angola, UNITA said on Friday.
A statement issued by the UNITA office in Rome said Savimbi's readiness for talks was in response to an appeal from U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
It said Annan had proposed a summit meeting in Italy "with the precise aim of overcoming the current deep crisis in the Angolan peace process".
"UNITA serves notice that its president is immediately available to attend such an event," the statement said.
Heavily armed UNITA soldiers are resisting a three-week-old government offensive in the diamond-rich northeast which threatens to rekindle civil war.
Diplomats say the fighting, the heaviest since the rivals signed a ceasefire in 1994 to end 20 years of conflict, could derail Angola's fragile peace process.

The government offensive coincided with the fall last month of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, who backed the UNITA rebels, and suggested that Luanda was seizing a chance to take back some UNITA territory, or possibly even destroy its rival.
The government and UNITA joined a power-sharing government in April, but Savimbi has refused to come to the capital Luanda.
